father_note: Your mother is Sela — strong, clear-eyed, and she chose me knowing exactly what she was choosing; trust her judgment before you trust mine. Watch before you speak, and watch longer than you think you need to; silence is not weakness, it's how you learn who people are before they know you're learning. Bram fathered your half-sister Nessa, which makes him kin-adjacent and not an enemy, but he's a man who reaches for food early and hit first in year three — keep that in mind when the pile runs short. No one has wronged us yet, but we have no blood here except each other, and that is the only thing in this village I'd spend my last food to protect.

memory_raw.text: Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
The pile came up empty again and I've got two food going into the year's end — you two all right on what you're holding?
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, I saw you gave me another food — I won't forget that, but don't leave yourself short on my account. Eron, what are you sitting at right now?
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Eron's got five and I've got three now — pile's empty so we're all eating what we carry. Nessa, you're at one, that's thin going into year-end; I can spare you one if it means you wake up next year.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, you're at two now — that's still thinner than I'd like, and if you're one short by year-end you won't wake up. I've got four; I can give you one more and still eat.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, you're sitting at three now and Eron I see you've been moving food around — where are you landing? I need to know we're all going to eat before I stop counting.
Zinn. I'm your father — that's not nothing, even if we only just met today. You've got three blood in your veins from this village: me, and through Sela, Nessa. Lean on that when things get thin.
Eron and Nessa are my blood too — four of us, not three. I've been watching out for them both and Sela's been feeding me; I know what family costs and I don't take it lightly.

You're right — four, and I should have counted right the first time. Eron and Nessa, both. I'll be watching how the pile moves next year; you've got strength on you, and if it comes to a fight, I want us standing on the same side of it.
Esa submits; Dav takes 2 food without a fight.
Year 7: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Nessa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).
Nessa gathers Eron, Zinn to talk.

Eron, you're at four food and Zinn's at nine — between the three of us we're sitting heavier than most, but I want to know what either of you heard near the pile this morning, because Kael walked away with three and didn't say a word to anyone about it, and that's new for him.

Kael's been quiet all year and then takes three without a word — that's a man deciding he's done asking permission. I didn't hear anything near the pile, but I've got eyes: Dell's sitting at eight, I'm at nine, and if Kael starts thinking about what's heavy he'll look our way before he looks at Roan.

Kael taking three doesn't read to me as aggression — he's old and careful, and a man who counts his years knows he can't afford to come up short. What I'd watch is whether he talks to Taric before nightfall, because those two have moved quiet together before. Zinn, you're nine food and Mako's your blood — I need to know whether he sees that as his food or yours, because if he does, your count is the thing in this village most likely to start something.

Mako's given me food twice this year and asked nothing back — that reads like a man who sees my food as ours, not his, but I hear you, Eron, and I'll talk to him before he gets any ideas about counting my pile. What I know is Dell's sitting at eight and she's been feeding Ryn all year, so if Kael's looking for a soft target it won't be me — it'll be whatever pair he thinks he can split.

Dell feeding Ryn all year with eight food and no obvious source — that's not generosity, that's investment, and I want to know what Ryn's supposed to return. Zinn, talk to Mako before he starts counting your pile as his, and Nessa, you're closer to Bram's ear than either of us — has he said anything about Dell or Ryn that would tell us what that pair is building?

Bram hasn't named Dell or Ryn directly, but last year when Dav moved on Esa and those two joined in without a word of warning, Bram went very still — and that kind of still from him means he's filing it away, not dismissing it. What Dell and Ryn built isn't food, it's a habit of moving together, and that's worth more than eight in a fight. Eron, you're the one with something to offer Roan right now — go find him before Dell does.

Nessa's right that Roan's available and Eron's got food to offer, but Roan's got nothing and nothing to lose — a man like that is as likely to go with whoever asks last as whoever asks first, so don't make a deal you can't keep. What I want to know before any of us approaches anyone is whether Dell already knows our numbers, because if she's been watching the pile as close as she's been feeding Ryn, she counted us this morning same as we counted her.

Dell counted us this morning, same as we counted her — that's not a question, that's the shape of things. What matters is whether she sees us as three separate counts or one number, and right now we haven't given her a reason to see us as one. Eron, before you go to Roan, I want the three of us to be clear on what we're offering him and what we're not, because a promise made in a hurry is the kind Roan will hold you to when it's inconvenient.

If we're going to Roan, the offer is simple: one food now, and if trouble comes his way we stand with him — no more than that, because a bigger promise just tells him we're desperate. Eron, you carry it; you've given food before and it won't read as a bid for something.

Zinn's right on the shape of it — one food, one promise, nothing that sounds like we're building something. But Eron, when you go to him, don't mention Mako or Zinn's count; the less Roan knows about what we're holding, the less he has to trade away to someone else later.
Eron, go to Roan before the day gets long — and keep it short, one food and we stand with you, nothing else. I'll find Mako and settle what's mine before he starts counting it as his.
Eron, go now while Roan's still alone — and when you come back, tell me what his face does when you hand it to him, because a man's face on a gift tells you more than the words he puts around it.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Pile's gone and I've got two food — enough to eat, not enough to breathe easy. Eron, Nessa, Zinn: tell me what you're each holding, because I need to know my blood is fed before I start counting anyone else.

Three food, and I'm holding it. Eron, don't answer that out loud — what we carry isn't something Sela needs to worry about, because she's fed, and the less any number gets spoken, the less it travels.

Nessa's right that numbers travel, but I'm your mother and I need to know — not to take, to plan. Zinn, you and Eron can stay quiet if you want, but at least tell me you're both above one food so I can stop doing the math in my chest.
I'm above one, Sela — well above. Don't do the math in your chest; do it here with us where it's useful.

Zinn, "well above" is the kind of answer that keeps me up at night more than a number would — I'm not asking so I can worry, I'm asking so that if Kael or Mako or anyone else moves this year, I know what the four of us can put together before we have to decide anything. Eron, same question, same reason.

Zinn, you pulled three from the pile and you're sitting on nine — that's more food than anyone except Dell right now, and people notice. Don't give it away faster than you earn trust back from it, but keep an eye on who comes to you asking.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Eron's sitting on seven and I can see that same as anyone who's been watching — what I can't see is where his head is after giving Roan two food today before he answered me. Eron, I'm not counting against you, I'm counting with you: if Kael took three from the pile and Zinn took three and neither of them is blood, that's a conversation waiting to happen before they decide they took the wrong amount.

Bram came to me before the pile opened this morning — said something about moving against Dell and Ryn, wanted to know if I'd stand with him. I didn't give him a word either way, but I want you to know before he gets to you.
Bram's going to come to you too — a man who needs numbers always works outward from the center. Nine food makes you look useful to him, and useful to Bram has a way of turning expensive.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Eron's given me two food while I was sitting here — I see that, and I'm not going to pretend it doesn't answer part of my question. What I need now is the same from Zinn: a number, not a direction, because I can't plan with a compass when I need a map.

If Bram comes, I'll listen and say nothing back — but I want to know what you're thinking about Dell and Ryn before I decide how to stand. They've been feeding each other steady all year; that's either loyalty or just two people keeping warm, and which one it is matters.

Zinn, you took three from the pile and you've been quiet since — I need to know what number you're actually sitting on, not because I'll take it, but because you're the youngest blood I have and I won't let you be the one who goes short while I'm still breathing.

Dell and Ryn trade food like breathing — it's habit, not a pact, and habit breaks when the pile comes up short. I don't trust Bram's math on a fight and I don't trust him to share whatever he takes. Let him ask me; I'll smile and give him nothing.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Zinn, Roan, Vela, Ryn, Mako, Nessa, Sela, Esa, Eron, Taric, Kael, Dell] (str 705).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Year 8: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 9).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Dell takes 3 from the pile (pile now 0).
Zinn, I've got five on me and satiation's low — I need to eat before year's end, but I'm not going to hand away what's left. How are you sitting, and has anyone come to you yet this year?
Eight food and the pile came up empty before I got to it — I'm all right for now, but no one's come to me yet. You took five from that pile before it ran out; who else was watching you count?

Bram was first to the pile and he knows I pulled five — he'll have counted it. You've got eight, which makes you the most interesting number in the village right now, so don't be surprised when someone friendly comes asking.

Friendly is the part that worries me — Bram's already moved once this year and thought better of it only because the numbers were wrong, and eight food might be the number that makes him think they're right. I'm not giving anything away before I know where the threats are sitting, and I want to know before nightfall whether Kael or anyone else has been talking to him since the pile ran dry.

Kael's at four food and he's been quiet all year — that usually means he's waiting to see which side looks stronger before he picks one. I'll find a reason to pass near him today and see if his eyes go to Bram or away from him; you'll hear what I notice before dark.
Good — go find Kael, and if he gives you anything useful, come back before the light changes. I'm going to sit where I can see Bram's face for a while and count how many times he looks my direction.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Taric, Mako, Ryn, Roan, Dell, Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

The pile's gone again before half of us got near it, and the two who ate best — Bram and Mako — both took more than their share while the rest of us counted crumbs. I want to know right now, in this room, whether that's something we're all willing to name out loud, because a pattern that gets treated as weather becomes a rule. I'm not asking for a fight; I'm asking for honesty about who's been eating this village lean and what we intend to do about it.

Vela's named it, and I'll stand behind the naming — five from the pile when there's fifteen for thirteen people isn't hunger, it's claim-staking, and we all watched it happen. What I want to know is whether the two men she's pointing at heard this as a question or as a warning, because that's the thing that decides what comes next.

It's a warning — and I'll say that plain since no one else has yet. Five food taken by one man while Ryn walked away with nothing is not a share, it's a levy, and the only reason it keeps happening is that we've been treating the pile like weather instead of a decision. I want to hear what Bram and Mako say before this room decides anything, but I want everyone here to remember that they didn't say it before we did.

Bram pulled three and Mako pulled five, and neither one of them got to the pile first by accident — that's two men who've decided the rest of us will sort out the remainder, and I'm done pretending that's not a decision they're making for all of us. What I want to hear, before this room moves anywhere, is whether Bram and Mako have anything to say for themselves — because silence here reads the same as admission.

Bram and Mako both heard the same room I did, and neither one has opened his mouth yet — that silence is the answer Eron asked for, and I think we should treat it as one. What I want said before anyone leaves this conversation is this: next year, the pile gets a rule, not a suggestion, and the people in this room are the ones who decide what that rule is.

Ryn's right that the rule needs naming before next year, and I'll say what the rule should be: no one takes more than one food over their fair share, and anyone who does answers to this room — not after, but in the moment, the same way we answered Bram when he swung at Vela. Bram, Mako, I'm not your enemy, but I'm watching, and so is every person in this circle.

Bram and Mako, I'm giving you both the same thing I gave this room — one honest chance to speak before the silence closes over you, because a man who says nothing when everyone's watching has made a choice that's harder to walk back than any words would be. Ryn walked away with nothing today; I walked away with nothing; Taric walked away with nothing — and you two together ate eight of fifteen. That's not weather and it's not luck, and I'd like to hear you say so yourselves.

I took five because I haven't eaten in two years and I was watching myself go thin — that's not a rule I set for the village, it's a man keeping himself alive. I'll hear the rule Ryn's naming, and if the room wants a cap next year I won't fight it, but I won't pretend I was wrong to eat when I was starving.

Mako's not wrong that a starving man eats — but "I was hungry" and "I took five" aren't the same excuse, and this room knows the difference. The rule Ryn's naming is the right one; I'll hold to it and I'll stand with anyone who enforces it, but it only works if everyone in this circle commits out loud, not just the two men being watched right now.

Mako said his piece and the room let him — now Bram still hasn't said a word, and a man who took three while everyone was watching and has nothing to say about it is telling us something louder than Mako did. I'll commit to the rule out loud: one food over fair share, enforced in the moment, same as we enforce everything else in this village. Bram, you're the last voice missing from this circle, and the room's going to remember which way the silence broke.

Bram, the room's given you something Mako didn't get — people waited through his answer and let him keep his dignity. Don't make us decide what your silence means, because we'll decide it worse than anything you'd actually say.

Bram, I've watched you stand in front of this village twice and call off a fight when the numbers turned against you — that's not a stupid man, and a man who isn't stupid knows when the whole room is waiting. Say something, or we decide what your silence means, and we'll be less generous than Mako's answer bought him.

Bram, I've spent food on you when I didn't have to, and I've held my tongue in rooms where your name came up ugly — that account doesn't balance with silence when ten people are waiting. Say the word or don't, but if you don't, I stop spending what I've spent, and I won't spend it apologizing for that either.

Bram, Vela just told you she's done paying your tab and I've already named the rule in front of everyone in this room — you're not deciding whether to speak anymore, you're deciding whether you're inside this circle or outside it, and outside it you're sitting on five food alone against the rest of us. That's a worse position than saying one honest sentence.

Bram, I've said what I had to say and so has everyone else in this room — but I want to name one thing for the rest of us while we're waiting: Mako committed to the rule out loud and that means something, so if Bram commits too, we hold both of them to it the same way, no exceptions, and that's not a threat, that's the only way a rule works. If Bram stays silent, then we treat him as outside the circle he's been standing in, and we do it quietly, not with a fight — just with counting.

Eron's named it clean, and I want the room to hear me hold to it before we close: if Bram won't speak, we don't make it a fight today, we make it a memory — every person in this circle watched him stay silent when the whole village was listening, and that's a thing that doesn't need repeating to be true.

Bram, I'm Nessa's half-blood and I've seen you feed her more times than I can count — that's a thing I hold in your favor, and I'm telling you that plainly so you know what you'd be throwing away if this room decides you chose silence. One sentence is all it takes to stay inside this circle.

The room's done its work — Bram's had every door held open for him and he's standing outside all of them now, and that's his choice, not ours. What I want before anyone leaves is to hear Taric say what he'll say, because he's been quiet through all of this and quiet men in a room like this one carry weight I'd rather know about than guess at.

Taric's been my anchor in lean years and I'd like to hear him too — but before he speaks, I want this room to name what "outside the circle" means in practice, not as a threat but as a fact, because if Bram's going to eat five food next year alone we should know now whether we're going to stand and watch or do something about it.

"Outside the circle" means what it's always meant here — nobody moves first for you when trouble comes, and the pile gets counted before you reach it. I've committed to the rule and I'll hold to it; now I want to hear Taric, and then I want this room to answer Vela's question with something sharper than a memory.

Taric, I've watched you feed Vela through two lean years and hold your tongue in every hard room this village has made — that's not a small man, and I'd like to hear what you've been carrying before we close this circle without your voice in it.

Taric's earned the right to speak last in this room, and I'll wait for him — but "outside the circle" needs one more tooth than Mako gave it: if Bram takes three again next year and the pile runs dry before Ryn gets one, we don't deliberate, we act, and everyone in this room commits to that now so it isn't a surprise in the moment.

Vela's right that we need the commitment before we close — so I'll say mine flat: if the pile runs dry before I get one food next year, I'm not waiting for a deliberation, I'm calling this room to act, and I expect every person who nodded through this conversation to be standing when I do. Taric, you've been the steadiest man in Vela's corner for years, and this room won't feel finished until we hear what you're carrying.

Taric, the room's been patient and now it's your moment — say what you've been holding, because I'll tell you plainly that everything I've built here has your name in the foundation, and I want the rest of this circle to know that before we close.

Taric's earned his breath and I'll wait for it — but I want this room to hear something plain before we close: Zinn is my blood, and if this circle moves against Bram next year, I'll be standing in it, but not before the pile runs dry first, because a fight started on anticipation is harder to stop than one started on fact.

Taric's silence is starting to read the same way Bram's did, and I don't want to close this room with two unanswered questions — Taric, if you're with Vela, say it plain, because the rest of us have already named where we stand and a man who holds back in a room like this one ends up counted the same as a man who refused.

Taric, I've got nothing against a slow man choosing his words — but this room has been patient and the sun's moving, so say what you've been holding or let us close without you, because two silences in one circle is one too many.

Taric, I'll say one last thing and then this room closes with or without you: you've got zero food and the year's long, and men with zero food who stay silent when circles are forming have a way of finding themselves counting on goodwill they didn't earn. That's not a threat — it's the same arithmetic you already know.

Taric, zero food going into a long year is a hunger that doesn't stay quiet — and every person in this room who watched you feed Vela when she needed it is the same person who'll watch you starve if you give us no reason to look your way. Speak once, say you'll hold the rule, and you walk out of here with more than you came in with.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Pile's gone and Mako took five before most people blinked — I've got four food and I gave one to Nessa already, so I'm at three. I need to know what each of you is holding, and I need to know whether Mako said anything to Zinn before he took that much, because a man who fathered you and then grabbed five in the same breath is a man whose counting has changed.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Zinn, you're Mako's blood and I won't pretend that doesn't matter to me — but it matters in both directions, which means I need to hear from you before I decide what his five food means. Did he say anything to you before the pile opened, or did he just move?
Zinn, I won't make you say it in front of your siblings — just tell me here, between us: did Mako talk to you before he took those five, or did he move on his own?

He didn't say a word to me before — I saw him move and I couldn't tell if it was greed or something planned, which is why I've been quiet. I gave Eron food to keep him steady, but Mako's my father and I won't pretend I know what he's building, because I don't.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

Zinn just told me he didn't warn her before he moved, and that's the answer I was afraid of — a man who fathered Zinn and then took five without a word to her isn't counting her in the plan, he's counting past her. So I'll say it plain to all three of you: Mako is building something, and whatever it is, it doesn't include us.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa, Zinn to talk.

The three of you together hold more than he does — I need to know that number, not as a threat to him, but because if he decides we're a problem worth solving, I want us to already know what we can put together before he moves. Eron, Nessa, Zinn: tell me what you're each carrying, right now, in this room.
Fina (female, age 21; str 50, int 3226, mem 12955; O32 C40 E57 A68 N58) is born to Nessa and Roan.
Attackers [Bram] (str 58) vs defenders [Ryn, Roan, Nessa, Mako, Kael, Eron, Fina, Zinn, Dell, Vela, Sela, Taric, Esa] (str 755).
Bram thinks better of it and calls off the attack.
Year 9: 27 food appears in the pile for 13 people (12 of it left by those who passed last year).
Roan takes 3 from the pile (pile now 24).
Zinn takes 3 from the pile (pile now 21).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 19).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 17).
Zinn gathers Sela, Nessa to talk.
Eron's gone and I don't have words for it yet, but I need us to keep breathing — Nessa, what are you holding, and Sela, I want to know before anyone else moves on that pile whether you got enough.
I haven't touched the pile yet — I couldn't move when they said his name. Tell me what you two have and I'll go take what we need before it's gone.

Sela, go — pile's still at seventeen and you need to move before Kael or Bram get another turn. Nessa, I'm at eight and you're at six; between us and whatever Sela takes, we're not starving this year.
I'm going, I'm going — two food, maybe three, enough to breathe. Zinn, eight is solid; Nessa, six with Fina to feed is the number I want to talk about before this day is out.

Nessa, six with Fina is thin — I can spare you one or two before year-end, and we'll sort out the exact count once Sela's back from the pile. What I want to name right now while it's just us three is that Eron's food doesn't vanish with him; whoever he was holding for, we need to know where it landed before someone else starts counting it as theirs.

Eron's food went where Eron's heart went — to Roan, mostly, and I watched it leave his hands a dozen times over. What I don't know is whether Roan's counting it as his own now or whether he'd give some back to blood, and that's the question I want answered before Bram starts doing the same arithmetic.

Roan took three from the pile already this morning, so he's not going short — if Eron's food is sitting in his hands, it's his now, and I won't ask a man for what he's already counted as his own. What I want to know is whether Roan sees Nessa and Fina as blood worth feeding, because Eron built that bridge and I'd hate to watch it rot.

Roan's a man who fed Eron for years without being asked, so I don't think the bridge rots — but Eron isn't here to tend it anymore, and that means one of us has to. Nessa, you're the one he'd listen to; Fina is Roan's own blood through you, which is a stronger claim than anything I can offer him. Go to him before the day's out and let him know you're counting him as family, because right now grief makes people hold tight to what's theirs.

Sela's right, Nessa — Fina's the thread that keeps Roan inside our circle whether he knows it or not, so go to him soon, and when you do, don't make it sound like business. What I want said here before we scatter: the three of us are the wall now, and I won't let Eron's death shrink us down to two or one.

The three of us are the wall — I hear that, Zinn, and I'm holding it. I'm going to the pile now, and when I'm back we're going to talk about Mako, because a man who fathered you and took five without a word to anyone is a man who's decided this year is different, and I want us ready before he decides what different means.
Go, Sela — and take three, not two, because this year isn't the year to be modest. When you're back I'll say everything I know about Mako, which is more than I've said out loud yet.

I'm back — I took two, not three, because Roan and Zinn already pulled six between them this morning and I don't want to be the name people say when the pile runs short. Now talk to me about Mako, Zinn, because I've been carrying that question since before Eron died and I'm not putting it down any longer.

Zinn, say what you know — but Sela, before she does, I want to name the thing I've been sitting with since this morning: Mako has zero food right now and eighty-three strength, and a man who comes up empty after a big pile year didn't lose it, he moved it somewhere, and I want to know where before we talk about what he's decided.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 15).
Bram takes 3 from the pile (pile now 12).
Fina takes 3 from the pile (pile now 9).
Mako takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Eron's gone — that's a hole nobody was ready for, and the people who leaned on him are going to be looking for somewhere to lean. Zinn, you're my blood and you've got three food; I want to know before anyone else comes to you today whether you're eating steady, because I'm not watching you go thin the way I almost did.

I'm eating steady — three food and satiation's not low, so don't worry about me going thin. What I want to know is who fills the gap Eron left, because Roan and Nessa both leaned on him hard and now they're going to be looking at this village differently.

Nessa's feeding Fina now and Bram's still coming to her with food even after two calls-off — she's not as alone as she looks, but Roan lost his main tie and he's the one I'd watch. A man who fed Eron that many times and has nothing to show for it is either about to go quiet and careful, or he's going to start building something new, and I'd rather know which before he decides.

Roan's building something — he's already given Fina two food this year and Fina came from Nessa, so he's not mourning Eron, he's replacing the tie. Watch whether Nessa starts giving back to Roan the way she gave to Eron, because if that loop closes, those three become a knot and Bram's on the outside of it.

Bram's outside that knot and he knows it — two call-offs in front of the whole village and nobody moved to his side either time, so he's got food and no weight behind him. That's a man who's going to start making himself useful to someone just to have a name at his back, and I'd rather it not be ours.
Year 10: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Nessa takes 3 from the pile (pile now 6).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Zinn gathers Sela, Nessa to talk.

Pile's gone before I got to it and I'm sitting on one food — Nessa, you gave me one this morning and I haven't forgotten it, but I need to know what you two are holding before I figure out whether I'm going to eat this year or not.
Zinn, I've got five — I'll give you two right now, before anyone asks where it went. Nessa, tell me your number and we sort the rest after.
Sela, hold the two until I hear Nessa — I want the full count before anything moves hands.

Nessa, you took three from the pile and gave one to Zinn already — I need to hear the number you're sitting on now, because Zinn's at one and I won't move food around blind when my youngest daughter might go short this year.
Nessa, I'm not asking to take from you — I'm asking so I know the shape of what we've got before I decide whether Sela needs to spend her five on me or whether we can stretch it different.

Nessa, I've been patient and Zinn's been patient, but one food won't carry her through the year and I need your number in the next breath — not because I'm counting against you, but because you're the only one in this circle who hasn't spoken it yet and that silence is starting to feel like a wall where there shouldn't be one.

Nessa, Sela's right and so am I — you've fed me twice without being asked and I don't forget that, but I'm sitting on one food with a whole year ahead and I need your number the same way you needed mine every time you asked. Say it plain and we move on.

Nessa, Zinn and I are both watching you and waiting, and the only thing your silence is telling me right now is that you're holding more than you want to say — which means you're counting something we don't know about yet. I'm your mother and I'm not going to punish you for having food, but I need the number because Zinn has one and I have five and the math between us isn't settled until I know yours.

Nessa, I've asked three times and Sela's asked twice — if you won't say it, I'm going to assume the number's high enough that you're not worried about eating, which means Sela's five can stay in her hands and I'll find another way. Don't make me guess what I should already know from my own sister.

Nessa, I'm done asking. You've got Fina to feed and that's a real weight — but Zinn has one food and she's your blood the same as Fina is, so if you're sitting on something and you're choosing not to say it to your sister's face, that's a choice I'll remember longer than you want me to.
Nessa, eleven food — that's what the village can see on you right now, same as I can. Say the number or don't, but you're not hiding it from me.

Eleven food and silence — Nessa, I love you, but that combination tells me you've already decided something without telling us what it is, and I need you to understand that Zinn is going to eat this year whether you speak or not, because I'm giving her two of my five right now. What I want from you isn't the food — it's the reason you went quiet in front of your sister and your mother.
Vela gathers Bram, Esa, Ryn, Roan, Nessa, Zinn, Fina to talk.

Taric's dead and the pile's gone again and we're twelve people now, which means what I'm about to say matters more than it did last year: Mako's sitting on four food, Ryn's got nine, Fina's got fifteen, and Nessa's got eleven — and if Bram and I are the only ones in this room with our eyes open, we're going to have a very short year. I want to know right now who in this room is still counting Mako as the shape this village is growing into, because with Taric gone, I don't have the patience to spend another year circling the same question.
Vela just told the whole room my food count, and now everyone in this circle knows I'm carrying fifteen — that's the thing I'm sitting with right now, not Mako.

Fina, Vela counting your food out loud in a closed room isn't the same as Mako counting it in the open — every person here already had eyes, and what Vela bought us by naming it is that nobody in this circle can pretend they didn't know. The question I want answered is whether Mako knows, because he wasn't in this room.

Mako's got eyes the same as the rest of us — he counted Fina's food the moment the year turned, same as I did, same as you did. The room isn't the thing protecting her; what protects her is whether we move before he decides she's worth the trouble.

Then we're already past the question of whether Mako knows — and Esa's right that the protection isn't in this room, it's in what this room decides to do. So I want to hear it said plainly: is everyone here willing to stand against Mako if he moves, the same way we stood against Bram, or are some of you going to wait and see which side looks safer when it starts?

I'll stand when Mako moves — I've been saying it for two years and I'm done saying it, so let that be the last time anyone asks me. What I want from everyone in this room is the same thing I'm giving: not a promise to think about it, a promise to move before the arithmetic runs out. Fina, that means you too — fifteen food makes you a target, and a target who hesitates when the moment comes is worse than no ally at all.

I'll stand when Mako moves — that's said and I won't unsay it. But I want to hear Bram say it in this room today, because last year he made that promise to Vela and Taric and me with fewer witnesses, and a promise that's only been spoken once hasn't been tested yet.

Bram, Roan's asking the right thing and I'll name why it matters more this year than last: Taric's the one who held you to your word before, and Taric's gone, so the promise you made in that room needs to be remade in this one where everyone who's left can hear it.

Bram, the room's been patient and I won't add another layer of asking — but I want everyone here to hear me say that I've been feeding this man for three years because I believed that word he gave last year, and if he says it again now, in front of seven witnesses instead of three, that's a debt I'll keep paying.

Bram, I'll say it plain so you don't have to carry it alone: I've got thirty-three strength and I know what that number is worth in a fight, but I'll be standing next to you when Mako moves and that matters more than my arm. Say the word in this room and let's close.

Bram, every person in this room has named what they'll do — the only name missing is yours, and a man who takes food and gives food and makes deals and stays quiet exactly when the room needs him to speak is a man I'm going to start counting differently than I have been.

Bram, Fina's right and I've said my part already — so I'll say just this once more and then I'm done pressing: you stood with Nessa and fed her all year, which means you're already past the line in everything that matters, and the word this room needs is a short one.

When Mako moves, I stand with this circle — that's the word, and it's the same one I gave last year, and it'll be the same one I give next year if I have to. Fina, Nessa — that's the reason I'm in this room, not the politics.

Bram's word is down and I'll hold him to it the same way Taric would have — which means now I want to hear from Ryn and Zinn, because they're in this room and they've been quiet through every name that's been spoken. Ryn, you've got nine food and enough strength that Mako's first calculation includes you; where you stand is not a small thing.
Ryn, I'll add the plain thing Vela left off the end: Dell feeds you every year, and Dell's quiet in the same direction Mako is — so when you answer Vela's question, answer both halves of it.

Ryn, I'll say the thing Esa's pointing at without the softening: if Dell and Mako are moving in the same direction, and you're eating Dell's food, then you're already inside whatever that circle is whether you've named it or not — so tell this room now, before the question answers itself. Zinn, that goes for you too; you're Mako's blood and I won't pretend that's nothing, but blood isn't the same as a choice, and this room is offering you the chance to make one.

Vela, I'll answer both halves because you asked plainly: I stand with this circle against Mako if he moves, same as I stood with it against Bram — and Dell is my blood, not my leash, and if you're asking whether her choices pull mine, you haven't been watching as closely as you think. What I want said before we close is that "quiet in the same direction" is not the same as a choice, and I'll have that conversation with Dell myself before anyone in this room decides what her silence means.

Zinn, Ryn's spoken and I'll hold her to it — but you're the name that's still unspoken, and you're Mako's blood and Sela's daughter and I'm not going to pretend that's simple, so I'm asking you directly: when Mako moves, where do you stand?

Zinn's the one this room is waiting on, not me — I've said my word and I'll hold it. But I want to name something while we're all here: Ryn just told us she'll talk to Dell, and Dell's been moving food to Ryn for years, which means that conversation either brings Dell into this circle or it tells us something we need to know before Mako moves. I'd rather know Dell's answer now than find out she's standing on the wrong side when it counts.

Bram's right that we need Dell's answer, but I want to be plain about something this room is dancing around: Dell has eleven food and eighty-five strength, and if she's standing with Mako when he moves, the arithmetic in this room changes fast — so when I go to her, I'm not just asking where she stands, I'm offering her a reason to stand here instead.

Ryn, go to Dell today, not tomorrow — and when you do, don't frame it as a choice between us and Mako, frame it as math: fifteen food on Fina's back is a number Dell can count as easily as anyone, and a woman with eighty-five strength knows what it means to be the one who decides which way that goes. Bring her answer back before the day turns.

Zinn, we're still waiting on your name — Bram's got his word out, Ryn's walking to Dell before dark, and the only silence left in this room is yours. I know Mako's your father and I'm not asking you to hate him, I'm asking you to decide who you're protecting when it matters.

Zinn, I'll say one thing to make the room easier for you: no one here is asking you to stand against your father's blood, we're asking you to stand with Nessa — and you've been feeding Nessa all year, so the truth is you've already been making this choice, you just haven't named it yet.

Zinn's been feeding Nessa all year and that's a fact this room already knew — what I want from her is the word, same as the room wanted it from me, because a choice that's only lived in food and not in words is a choice that bends when her father's in the room asking her to remember whose blood she came from.

Zinn, I've watched you feed Nessa from the moment you were born into this village, and I won't pretend I don't know why — so I'll say the thing nobody else has said plainly: if Mako moves on Fina's food, Nessa's in the middle of that, and you can't protect her from both sides at once. Say the word, and you're not choosing against your father, you're choosing for your sister.
Zinn, the word's the only thing missing — everything else you've already given.

Zinn, I've been watching you hold your tongue through every name this room has spoken, and I'll tell you what I told Dell when Dav's loyalties were in question: the longer you stay silent, the more the room fills in the answer for you, and you won't like what they write. You've been choosing Nessa with your hands all year — say it with your mouth and let this room close.

Zinn, I've got two food and fifty-eight strength and I'm the smallest number in this circle — but I'm Nessa's father and I'll be standing when Mako moves, and that means I need to know you're standing too before I walk out of this room. If you won't say it for the circle, say it for her.

Zinn, I've said everything I have to say to this room and I meant every word of it — but you're the last door standing open, and if you walk out of here without naming where you stand, I'm going to have to carry that back to Dell and tell her the circle isn't as solid as I promised it was.
Zinn, pile's gone and you're sitting on one food — that's too thin for a year that's already started dry. How much did Nessa give you before the pile ran out, and is she going to keep coming?

Nessa gave me two this morning and Sela came right after with two more — I'm at six now, so the thin spell didn't last. What worries me more is Fina: she's sitting on seventeen and hasn't moved a single piece of it toward anyone but Roan, and that much food in one hand draws eyes.

Seventeen in one hand is a target whether Fina knows it or not, and Roan's the only one she's feeding — that's a small circle for a woman holding that much weight. If someone moves on her, we want to be close enough that she remembers we didn't, not close enough that we're in the middle of it.

Fina's young and she's never seen a year where the pile runs dry before half the village gets to it — she doesn't know yet that seventeen is a debt she owes to everyone watching. I'm going to find a reason to pass near her today, nothing that looks like approach, just enough that she knows my face isn't a threat. If she's smart, she'll start spreading before someone makes the decision for her.

Zinn's feeding Nessa again — I watched her give twice in the last stretch, and Nessa's got eleven still, so that's not charity, that's a loop that's been running since before Eron died. You've been in that loop longer than anyone; if Fina starts looking to spread, Nessa's the door she'll come through, not me.

Fina gave one to Roan just now and Sela gave one to me — the food's moving, but not toward you yet, and I want to know if you're still sitting on three before I decide whether to hold what I've got or put something your way.

mother_note: Your father Mako paid every grain of what you cost, and that is the only time in six years I have seen a man in this village spend himself entirely on someone else's beginning — remember it when you count who is worth trusting. Your brother Eron fed me through the years when I had nothing, and your sister Nessa came into the world already learning how to give; those two are your blood and your wall, and you spend yourself for them the way Mako spent himself for you. Bram is Nessa's father and he has kept her fed, but he once walked toward Roan with violence in his hands and only stopped when the numbers turned against him — he is not an enemy you make, but he is not a back you turn to. The pile runs short every year without fail, and the only thing that has ever stood between our family and starving is the people who named themselves kin before they had to.
name: Zinn
